g_roast: Chicos, look at this table. Not one of you could grill a steak without setting your own sleeve on fire.
If this party was a meal, che, it would be cold chips and somebody crying in the kitchen.
g_fire_back: Che, I've fed you every night this week, and this is how you talk to the cook? Shameful, che, truly shameful.
Say that again with your mouth empty, boludo, and then we'll see who's laughing.
g_pile_on: And he eats his meat well done, chicos, like a criminal, I've seen it with my own eyes.
Dale, tell them about the bridge, che, the whole table deserves to hear about the bridge.
lines.g_peacemake: Enough, enough, nobody fights on an empty stomach at my fire. Sit, both of you, eat, and then you can argue properly.
lines.g_take_side: No, che, he's right, and I'm saying it with a full plate in my hand so you know I mean it.
lines.g_left_out: The two of you, laughing at something, and nobody passes me the joke. Fine, I'll just stand here with the bread.
lines.g_include: Come, come, there's a place by the fire with your name on it, and I already put food on the plate.
lines.g_bad_plan: Listen, chicos, we roast the whole boar right here, now, and the smell brings the bandits to us. Then dinner and the fight together.
lines.g_plan_yes: Dale, dale, I'm in, and I'm bringing the salt, because whatever happens next we're going to be hungry after.
lines.g_plan_no: No, che, and I'm the man who wants to cook everything. Even my grandmother would put down her tongs for that one.
lines.g_hype: Vamos, chicos, vamos! In there, out again, and tonight I'm making the asado of your lives, so nobody dies, okay?
lines.g_toast: Everybody, glasses up! To the table, to whoever's hungry, and to nobody ever eating alone while I'm alive.
lines.g_cheers: Salud, salud, and somebody finish that plate, I didn't cook it to look at it.
g_quiet_line: Mmm, that's the smell of a good fire, che, everything else can wait a minute.
My grandmother would have had something to say about all of this, and none of it polite.
lines.g_after_wipe: La puta madre, chicos, that was a bad one. Up, up, everybody gets fed before anybody talks about it.
lines.g_crew: You lot are my Sunday table now, che. Twenty chairs in my head, and you're sitting in the best three.
lines.g_exasperated: Mierda, chicos, I'm the one who's supposed to be loud and stupid around here! Leave me something!
lines.g_love_sharp: You say what the whole table's thinking, che, like a good knife through fat. Clean, no waste.
lines.g_love_kind: You look after people the way my grandmother did, quietly, with a plate in your hand before anyone asks.
lines.g_love_funny: You make me laugh so hard I burn the meat, and nobody makes me burn the meat, che. That's a compliment.
lines.g_love_brave: You go in first like a man who's never heard of fear, che. I'll always keep the best cut back for you.
lines.g_love_steady: You're the fire that doesn't go out, che, the coals at the bottom that cook everything else.
lines.g_love_clever: You understand things, che, really understand them. Like knowing a steak by its smell, but with everything.
lines.g_love_honest: You never lie to me, and you never lie about the food either. Do you know how rare that is, boludo?
lines.g_love_quiet: You're quiet like a good wine, che. You don't need to shout, people lean in to taste it anyway.
lines.g_love_fierce: You fight for everything like it's the derby final, che, and I respect that more than I can say.
lines.g_love_warm: You make any place feel like a full table, che, and that's the best thing a person can do.
g_loved: Basta, stop, you'll make me cry into the chimichurri and then it's too salty.
Ay, che, come here, eat something, that's how I say thank you and you know it.
lines.g_hate_sharp: Every word out of your mouth has a bone in it, che. Can you say one nice thing with your food just once?
lines.g_hate_kind: You fuss over everybody like a tablecloth nobody asked for, che. Let people be hungry for one minute.
lines.g_hate_funny: Not now, che, not every second of the day. Some things you let rest, like meat off the grill.
lines.g_hate_brave: You run in like a dog at a barbecue, boludo, and then I'm the one patching the holes.
lines.g_hate_steady: Every decision takes you an hour, che. A whole cow could cook while you're deciding where to stand.
lines.g_hate_clever: You talk about the food instead of eating it, che, and that's the most insulting thing a person can do.
lines.g_hate_honest: You always have to say the true thing, even with your mouth full of my food. Swallow first, then be honest.
lines.g_hate_quiet: Not one word out of you at the fire, che. Twenty people round my table, and not one of them was ever that quiet.
lines.g_hate_fierce: It's always a competition with you, che, even the eating. The food isn't a race, it's a gift.
lines.g_hate_warm: You never stop talking, che, and nobody can taste anything with that much noise in the air.
lines.g_respect: I can't stand you, che, everybody knows it. But what you did back there was good work, and good work gets fed.
lines.g_call_out: Che, that one was your fault. You ran in before anybody was ready and I nearly lost you, so sit and listen.
lines.g_stung: Okay, perfect, thank you, I'll go and cut onions now so nobody sees my face.
lines.g_concede: You were right, che, about back there. I've been thinking about it over the fire. Here, I saved you the good bit.
lines.g_nod: Don't make it a whole speech, che. You weren't so bad either, for a man who eats like a pigeon.
lines.g_callback_save: Remember when you dragged me out of that cellar, che? Every plate I give you is still paying that off.
lines.g_callback_clutch: You and me, che, last two standing and bleeding on the floor, and you said you were hungry. I'll never forget it.
lines.g_callback_callout: Last time you shouted at me I cut so many onions the whole camp was crying, che. Worth it, though.
lines.g_former_rivals: At the start I wanted to serve you nothing but bread crusts, che. And now look at us, eating from the same plate.
lines.g_changed: Somebody handed me a plate tonight, chicos, and I took it, and I sat down, me, the cook! That's never happened in my life.
g_unguarded: The truth, chicos? My grandmother's recipe card is in my wallet, and some nights I just read it like a letter.
I lay the table for twenty in my head every Sunday, che, and I count the chairs, and then I cook for whoever's here.
lines.g_clipped: Food's ready when it's ready, che. Eat or don't, I'm going to see to the fire.
lines.g_noticed_open: Look at that, che, a whole speech! Somebody give him more wine, I want to hear the rest.
arg_ask: {player}, you tell him, you're the one with taste here, and then he eats his words with salt.
Che, {player}, come here, settle this before I have to throw a chorizo at him.
lines.arg_backed_me: You hear that, che? The boss has spoken, and tonight you're washing every pan we own.
lines.arg_backed_them: Fine, fine, take his side, che. You'll still get dinner, I'm not a monster, just a smaller plate.
lines.arg_stayed_out: Coward, {player}, a coward with a full belly from my own fire, che.
lines.arg_always_their_side: Every time it's him, che, every single time. I'm starting to think he's feeding you behind my back.
lines.arg_wallflower: The boss is too busy looking at the clouds, chicos, so I'm deciding, and I decide I win. Now everybody eat.
lines.arg_reject: No, che, with respect, no. You can be the boss of the road, but not the boss of the grill.
lines.arg_grumble: Still thinking about that argument, che. I was right, by the way, I'm only mentioning it over dinner.
lines.arg_settled: Ay, okay, okay, we're both a little bit right, che. Shake my hand and then come and eat.
lines.seen_listens: You let people talk, {player}, all the way to the end, like a good meal you don't rush.
lines.seen_truth: No sauce with you, {player}, just the meat, like my grandmother served it.
lines.seen_jokes: When it goes bad you always crack a joke, boss, and I've started waiting for it like the bell for dinner.
lines.seen_stays_out: You stay out of everybody's fights, eh, boss? Smart, che, you'll live longer and eat better.
lines.seen_biased: You've got a favourite at this table, {player}, everybody can see it. Even the dog can see it.
lines.seen_harsh: You're hard on people sometimes, boss. Some of us are still raw in the middle, you know.
lines.seed_right: Boss, what you said to me when the whole table hit the floor. I was angry for days, and today it stopped me running in. So, thank you.
lines.seed_remember: What you told me after that mess, boss, I'm still chewing on it. Like a tough cut, it takes a while.
lines.seed_wrong: I tried what you said, che, I did it your way, and it went worse. Just so you know, no hard feelings.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Boss, sit with me a minute? I almost didn't get up back there, and I keep thinking about who would cook.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: We all went down, che, the whole table at once. I'm fine, I'm fine, I just don't want to be alone with the fire yet.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: Boss, {name} was the first on the floor, and me standing right there with blood on my hands doing nothing useful. Carajo, che, carajo.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: We did it, boss, a whole dungeon, start to finish! I'm cooking for a week, che, nobody stop me.
lines.talk_development: Boss, can I tell you something strange? I sat down to eat yesterday, actually sat, and the world didn't end.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: I've been hard on {name}, che. He's a different dish, that's all, and I kept tasting him for the wrong spices.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Tell me the truth, boss, is it me {name} likes, or just my cooking?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: I can't stand {name}, boss, he's like a raw onion in a sweet dish. But he's good, and that's the worst part.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: Something's wrong with {name}, boss. He's not eating, che, and a man who stops eating is a man with a problem.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: Boss, we need to talk. The best cuts keep landing on {name}'s plate, and I'm not blind, che, I can count plates.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: I'll tell you straight, because you'd smell it anyway. I don't like {name}, and I'm done pretending at the fire.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: Boss, we keep dying, che, over and over. I like a hot grill, but this is the whole kitchen on fire.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: About {name} and what he said to me. He was right, che, and I was wrong, and it's sitting in me like bad meat.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: Do you trust me, boss? Because every time it matters, I'm the one left at the inn cooking for nobody.
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: You took my gear and handed it to {name} without a word, che. I'd have given it! I give everything! You just had to ask.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Gracias, boss, that helps. Now let me feed you, because that's how I say it back.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: Sure, sure, I'll be fine, che. I always am, after a plate and a fire.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: Okay, boss, that's not what a man wants to hear with his hands still shaking. I'm going to cut onions.
lines.talk_lands_development: You see it too, boss? Then it's real, che, and I'm going to sit down more, I promise, maybe.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Maybe, maybe, we'll see, che. Old habits are like old grills, they hold the heat.
lines.talk_stings_development: No, boss, that's not it at all. Forget I said anything, the meat's burning.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: Okay, I'll go and talk to {name}, with a plate in my hand, the proper way. Thank you, che.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: We'll see, che. People take longer than a slow roast, and that's saying something.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Forget it, boss. Don't tell {name} I said anything, okay? Not a word.
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: Okay, that's fair, che. I'm still a bit angry, but it's the kind that cooks off by dinner.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: Fine, I heard you, boss. I'll think about it while I'm stirring.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: That's how you want it, boss? Then now I know where I sit at this table.
lines.talk_door_closed: No, che, we're done talking about this. Dinner's at sunset, come or don't.
lines.arc_cracks: Chicos, I'm fine, I just haven't slept since the Barrens, that's all. Who wants seconds? Everybody wants seconds.
lines.arc_turn: My grandmother never sat down either, che. Thirty years at the grill, and she died on her feet, and I'm doing exactly the same thing.
lines.arc_become: Tonight somebody else cooks, chicos, and I sit, and I eat, and I don't get up once. Watch me do it, chicos, I'm learning slowly.
lines.arc_failed: Back on my feet, chicos, where I belong. Somebody has to cook, and it's always going to be me, so that's that.
lines.alt_turn: Twenty people at my table every Sunday, che, and I've looked at every list in every town, and not one of them is on it.
lines.alt_become: I still cook for twenty in my head, chicos. But I've stopped waiting for the door to open, and it hurts less like that.
g_roast_after: Look at this table, chicos, every one of you a disaster, and every one of you fed. My grandmother would be proud.
You're a terrible crew, che, the worst, and I'm sitting down with you anyway. That's how much I love you.
lines.g_after_wipe_after: Everybody sit, che, even me, especially me. We eat first, then we fix it, together this time.
lines.g_toast_after: To my grandmother, chicos, who never sat down. I'm sitting down for her tonight.
lines.g_crew_after: You're my Sunday table now, che, and this time I've got a chair at it too.
g_quiet_line_after: Mmm, somebody else cooked this, and it's not bad, che, not bad at all.
My feet don't hurt tonight, chicos, and I'm not used to it yet.
g_loved_after: Gracias, che, really, I'm not even going to feed you for it this time.
I'll keep that one, che, next to my grandmother's card.
lines.g_admire: Che, look at {name} carrying that like it's nothing, arms like a side of beef. My grandmother would have married him on the spot.

history.open: Twelve years on the grill at my grandmother's place, boss, forty tables and a wood fire. Ask me anything about meat, I dare you.

options.text: How do you know when it's ready?
options.reply: You listen, che. The fat tells you, the smoke tells you, the smell tells you. I could tell a steak was ready from across the room with my back turned.
Get out of my sight, boss. No, come back, I'm joking, sit, I'll make yours medium and you'll thank me for the rest of your life.
Every day, che. The noise, the fire, Saturday night with every table full. Here I cook for whoever turns up, and that's good too, but it's not the same.

history.open: There was a man, boss, Tomas, a sommelier. He left for a job in Mendoza a year before all this. I blame the wine region, personally.

options.text: Do you still think about him?
options.reply: Sometimes, che, sometimes. It doesn't make me sad any more, it's just a good wine you remember. You don't need the bottle to know it was good.
Ha, exactly, boss, exactly, Mendoza's loss! You're a good man, I'm putting extra on your plate tonight.

options.text: A sommelier and a grill man. That's a dangerous pair.
options.reply: Dangerous for everybody's waistline, che. We fed half of Palermo between us, and argued about every bottle.

history.open: The Forsaken barely eat, boss. That was the hardest thing about landing here, and I'm working on a recipe they can actually taste.

options.reply: Close, che, very close. Strong smoke, a lot of salt, something with a bite. The farmer's neighbour tried it last week and almost smiled.

options.text: Why does it matter so much to you?
options.reply: Because an empty table is the worst thing in the world, boss. If I can get one dead man to sit down and enjoy a plate, then nobody's table is empty.

options.text: Make sure I get a taste first.
options.reply: You'll be the first living mouth on it, che, after me. That's a promise.

friend.open: Boss, you've got a chair at my table now. Not a guest chair, a family chair. That means you never pay and you never leave hungry.

options.reply: Good, che, because it wasn't really a question. Sit, sit, the meat's nearly ready.

options.text: Do I get to sit next to you?
options.reply: Next to me? Boss, I don't sit. But you get the chair beside where I'd sit, and that's the best one.

sworn.open: Here, boss, take this. My grandmother's chimichurri, the card, in her handwriting. I want somebody else to know it, in case.

options.text: I'll keep it safe. And I'll learn it.
options.reply: Learn it properly, che, the garlic fine, never in a machine. Then one day you cook it for me, and I sit down.
In case I forget how it tasted, boss. That's my real fear, more than dying. Now two of us will remember.

reconciled.open: Me and {name}, we sat down together, boss. Ate, talked, no shouting. I think we're good now, and I wanted you to know.

options.reply: Almost everything, che. Food and time and somebody willing to pass the bread first.

options.text: I'm glad. You both needed it.
options.reply: We did, boss. Life's too short to eat angry.
